# `silk/collections/list`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Growable lists that own their elements, with stable sorting and binary search.

## When to use
Use [`List`](#List) when the number of elements is known only at runtime, or the sequence must grow.
Use a fixed array `[T; N]` when the length is part of the type. Use `silk.collections.bytes.Bytes` for a
block of bytes that does not grow.

## Details
[`List.make`](#List.impl.make) does not allocate. The first growth allocates space for four elements, and each
later growth doubles the capacity. Use [`List.reserve`](#List.impl.reserve) or [`List.reserveExact`](#List.impl.reserveExact) to allocate
before a sequence of appends. Growth copies the elements into new storage before it releases the
old storage. Thus a failed [`List.append`](#List.impl.append) or [`List.reserve`](#List.impl.reserve) leaves the list unchanged.

[`List.remove`](#List.impl.remove), [`List.clear`](#List.impl.clear), and [`List.truncate`](#List.impl.truncate) drop the elements that they remove and
keep the capacity. Dropping a list drops each element and then releases the storage.

[`List.sort`](#List.impl.sort) is stable and works for elements that are not `Copy`. It allocates temporary
storage. [`List.binarySearch`](#List.impl.binarySearch) needs a sorted list and returns the lowest index of equal
elements.

## Gotchas
[`List.get`](#List.impl.get), [`List.set`](#List.impl.set), and [`List.remove`](#List.impl.remove) trap if the index is not less than the length.
[`List.insert`](#List.impl.insert) traps if the index is more than the length. [`List.get`](#List.impl.get) copies the element, so
it needs `T: Copy`. Use [`List.asSlice`](#List.impl.asSlice) to borrow an element that is not `Copy`.

## Examples
### Grow and change a list
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.collections.list { List }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut values = List<i32>.make()
  run List<i32>.append(&mut values, 10) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run List<i32>.append(&mut values, 30) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run List<i32>.insert(&mut values, 1, 20) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  List<i32>.set(&mut values, 2, 22)
  let removed = List<i32>.remove(&mut values, 0)

  // The list is now [20, 22].
  if removed != 10 || List<i32>.get(&values, 0) + List<i32>.get(&values, 1) != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

### Sort values and find the first equal value
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.num.usize
import silk.collections.list { List }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut values = List<i32>.make()
  run List<i32>.append(&mut values, 36) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run List<i32>.append(&mut values, 3) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run List<i32>.append(&mut values, 3) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run List<i32>.sort(&mut values) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)

  // The list is now [3, 3, 36]. The search returns the first 3.
  let found = List<i32>.binarySearch(&values, 3) |> Option<usize>.unwrapOr(usize.MAX)
  if found != usize.ZERO || List<i32>.get(&values, 2) != 36 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## `List`

```silk
pub struct List<T>
```

A growable list that owns its elements in one contiguous allocation.

### Details

The length is the number of elements in the list. The capacity is the number of elements that
fit before the next growth. Dropping a list drops each element and then releases the storage. A
list is affine. Copy it element by element if a second list is necessary.

[`List.make`](#List.impl.make) does not allocate. The first growth allocates space for four elements, and each
later growth doubles the capacity. Use [`List.makeWithCapacity`](#List.impl.makeWithCapacity) to create a list with its
storage in one call, or [`List.reserve`](#List.impl.reserve) and [`List.reserveExact`](#List.impl.reserveExact) to allocate before a sequence
of appends. Growth copies the elements into new storage before it releases the old storage, so a
failed [`List.append`](#List.impl.append) or [`List.reserve`](#List.impl.reserve) leaves the list unchanged. [`List.remove`](#List.impl.remove),
[`List.clear`](#List.impl.clear), and [`List.truncate`](#List.impl.truncate) drop the elements that they remove and keep the capacity,
so a list cleared in a loop reuses its storage. [`List.clearAndFree`](#List.impl.clearAndFree) also releases the storage,
and [`List.shrinkToFit`](#List.impl.shrinkToFit) releases only the capacity beyond the length.

[`List.sort`](#List.impl.sort) is stable, works for elements that are not `Copy`, and allocates temporary
storage. [`List.binarySearch`](#List.impl.binarySearch) needs a sorted list and returns the lowest index of equal
elements.

### Gotchas

[`List.get`](#List.impl.get), [`List.set`](#List.impl.set), and [`List.remove`](#List.impl.remove) trap if the index is not less than the length.
[`List.insert`](#List.impl.insert) traps if the index is more than the length. [`List.get`](#List.impl.get) copies the element, so
it needs `T: Copy`. Use [`List.asSlice`](#List.impl.asSlice) to borrow an element that is not `Copy`.

<a id="List.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make() -> List<T>
```

Returns an empty list. This function does not allocate.

#### Details

The capacity is 0. The first [`List.append`](#List.impl.append), [`List.insert`](#List.impl.insert), or [`List.reserve`](#List.impl.reserve) allocates.

<a id="List.impl.makeWithCapacity"></a>

### Associated function `makeWithCapacity`

```silk
pub effect fn makeWithCapacity(capacity: usize) -> List<T> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns an empty list with storage for exactly `capacity` elements.

#### When to use

Use `makeWithCapacity` when the number of elements is known or can be estimated before the
appends, so that the list allocates once instead of growing step by step.

#### Details

The length is 0 and the capacity is `capacity`. Appends up to that capacity do not allocate.
A `capacity` of 0 does not allocate and gives the same list as [`List.make`](#List.impl.make).

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the size of `capacity` elements overflows, or the `Allocator` cannot
  supply the storage.

#### Examples
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.collections.list { List }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut values = run List<u32>.makeWithCapacity(16) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run List<u32>.append(&mut values, 7) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if List<u32>.length(&values) != 1 || List<u32>.capacity(&values) != 16 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="List.impl.asSlice"></a>

### Method `asSlice`

```silk
pub fn asSlice(self: &Self) -> &[T]
```

Returns a shared borrow of all elements as a slice, in list order.

#### When to use

Use `asSlice` to read elements that are not `Copy`, or to give the elements to a function that
takes `&[T]`.

#### Gotchas

The slice borrows the list. The compiler rejects a change to the list, such as an append,
while the slice is live.

<a id="List.impl.asMutSlice"></a>

### Method `asMutSlice`

```silk
pub fn asMutSlice(self: &mut Self) -> &mut [T]
```

Returns an exclusive borrow of all elements as a slice, in list order.

#### When to use

Use `asMutSlice` to change elements in place, such as in a loop over all elements.

#### Gotchas

The slice cannot change the length. The compiler rejects other uses of the list while the
slice is live.

<a id="List.impl.append"></a>

### Method `append`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn append<'env>(self: &mut Self, value: T) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds `value` at the end of the list.

#### Details

The list takes ownership of `value`. If the list is full, it grows: the first growth allocates
space for four elements, and each later growth doubles the capacity.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the new storage. The list does not
  change.

<a id="List.impl.insert"></a>

### Method `insert`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn insert<'env>(self: &mut Self, index: usize, value: T) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Inserts `value` at position `index` and moves the elements from `index` onward one position to
the right.

#### Details

`index` equal to [`List.length`](#List.impl.length) appends the value. The move of the later elements takes time
in proportion to their number. `T` does not need to be `Copy`.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the new storage. The list does not
  change.

#### Gotchas

If `index` is more than [`List.length`](#List.impl.length), the program traps.

```silk
pub fn get<T: Copy>(self: &Self, index: usize) -> T
```

Returns a copy of the element at position `index`.

#### When to use

Use `get` when `T` is `Copy`. Use [`List.asSlice`](#List.impl.asSlice) to borrow an element that is not `Copy`.

#### Gotchas

If `index` is not less than [`List.length`](#List.impl.length), the program traps.

### Method `pop`

```silk
pub fn pop(self: &mut Self) -> Option<T>
```

Removes the last element and returns it. Returns `None` if the list is empty.

<a id="List.impl.remove"></a>

### Method `remove`

```silk
pub fn remove(self: &mut Self, index: usize) -> T
```

Removes the element at position `index`, returns it, and moves the later elements one position
to the left.

#### Details

The caller owns the returned element. The capacity does not change. Use [`List.pop`](#List.impl.pop) to remove
the last element without a move of other elements.

#### Gotchas

If `index` is not less than [`List.length`](#List.impl.length), the program traps.

<a id="List.impl.clear"></a>

### Method `clear`

```silk
pub fn clear(self: &mut Self) -> ()
```

Drops all elements and sets the length to 0. The capacity does not change.

#### When to use

Use `clear` to reuse a list, such as a buffer filled again on each pass of a loop: later
appends up to the old capacity do not allocate. Use [`List.clearAndFree`](#List.impl.clearAndFree) to also release the
storage.

<a id="List.impl.clearAndFree"></a>

### Method `clearAndFree`

```silk
pub fn clearAndFree(self: &mut Self) -> ()
```

Drops all elements and releases the storage. The length and the capacity become 0.

#### When to use

Use `clearAndFree` when the list stays alive but its storage is no longer needed, such as a
large buffer that is kept for rare later use. Use [`List.clear`](#List.impl.clear) to keep the storage for
reuse.

#### Details

This function does not allocate and does not need an `Allocator`. The next append allocates
again, as on a list from [`List.make`](#List.impl.make).

### Method `truncate`

```silk
pub fn truncate(self: &mut Self, length: usize) -> ()
```

Drops the elements from position `length` to the end. The capacity does not change.

#### Details

If `length` is more than or equal to the current length, this function does nothing.


Replaces the element at position `index` with `value` and drops the old element.

<a id="List.impl.reserve"></a>

### Method `reserve`

```silk
pub effect fn reserve(self: &mut Self, additional: usize) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Makes sure that at least `additional` more elements fit without another allocation.

#### When to use

Use `reserve` before a loop of appends when the number of new elements is known. Use
[`List.reserveExact`](#List.impl.reserveExact) when the final length is known and extra capacity is not wanted.

#### Details

If the capacity is already sufficient, this function does nothing. Otherwise, it grows the
capacity by doubling until the elements fit. The length does not change.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if `length + additional` overflows `usize`, or the `Allocator` cannot
  supply the new storage. The list does not change.

<a id="List.impl.reserveExact"></a>

### Method `reserveExact`

```silk
pub effect fn reserveExact(self: &mut Self, additional: usize) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Makes sure that at least `additional` more elements fit, with no extra capacity.

#### When to use

Use `reserveExact` when the final length is known, such as before a copy of a slice. Use
[`List.reserve`](#List.impl.reserve) when more appends can follow.

#### Details

If the capacity is already sufficient, this function does nothing and does not shrink the
storage. Otherwise, it allocates storage for exactly `length + additional` elements. The
length does not change.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if `length + additional` overflows `usize`, or the `Allocator` cannot
  supply the new storage. The list does not change.

<a id="List.impl.shrinkToFit"></a>

### Method `shrinkToFit`

```silk
pub effect fn shrinkToFit(self: &mut Self) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Releases the capacity beyond the length.

#### When to use

Use `shrinkToFit` on a list that is complete and kept for a long time, so that the spare room
left by doubling growth does not stay allocated.

#### Details

If the capacity equals the length, this function does nothing. If the list is empty, it
releases the storage, and the capacity becomes 0. Otherwise, it moves the elements into
storage for exactly the length. The length does not change.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the new storage. The list does not
  change. An empty list never fails.

<a id="List.impl.sort"></a>

### Method `sort`

```silk
pub effect fn sort<T: Order>(self: &mut Self) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Sorts the elements in place, in ascending order of the `Order` conformance of `T`.

#### Details

The sort is stable: equal elements keep their order. The result is deterministic. The sort
works for elements that are not `Copy`. It allocates temporary storage from the active
`Allocator`.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the temporary storage. The list does not
  change.

<a id="List.impl.binarySearch"></a>

### Method `binarySearch`

```silk
pub fn binarySearch<T: Order>(self: &Self, target: T) -> Option<usize>
```

Returns the position of an element equal to `target` in a sorted list, or `None` if no element
is equal.

#### Details

If more than one element is equal to `target`, the result is the lowest position. The search
takes time in proportion to the logarithm of the length. This function consumes `target` and
does not change the list.

#### Gotchas

The list must be sorted in ascending order by the same `Order` conformance, for example by
[`List.sort`](#List.impl.sort). For a list that is not sorted, the result has no meaning.

<a id="List.impl.appendBytes"></a>

### Method `appendBytes`

```silk
pub effect fn appendBytes(self: &mut List<u8>, values: &[u8]) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds a copy of each byte of `values` at the end of the list, in order.

#### When to use

Use `appendBytes` to add many bytes at once. It copies the bytes in one operation, which is
faster than one [`List.append`](#List.impl.append) for each byte. [`List.appendSlice`](#List.impl.appendSlice) does the same for any
`Copy` element type.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the new storage. The list does not
  change.

<a id="List.impl.appendSlice"></a>

### Method `appendSlice`

```silk
pub effect fn appendSlice<T: Copy>(self: &mut Self, values: &[T]) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds a copy of each element of `values` at the end of the list, in order.

#### When to use

Use `appendSlice` to add many elements at once. It grows the list once and copies the elements
in one operation, which is faster than one [`List.append`](#List.impl.append) for each element.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the new storage. The list does not
  change.

#### Examples
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.collections.list { List }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut values = List<u16>.make()
  let more: [u16; 2] = [8, 9]
  run List<u16>.appendSlice(&mut values, &more) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if List<u16>.length(&values) != 2 || List<u16>.get(&values, 1) != 9 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="List.impl.appendRepeated"></a>

### Method `appendRepeated`

```silk
pub effect fn appendRepeated<T: Copy>(self: &mut Self, value: T, count: usize) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds `count` copies of `value` at the end of the list.

#### Details

The list grows at most once, and the copies are written in one tight loop with no call or
capacity check for each element. For `u8` the loop compiles to a `memset`. A `count` of 0 does
nothing and does not allocate.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if `length + count` overflows `usize`, or the `Allocator` cannot supply
  the new storage. The list does not change.

#### Examples
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.collections.list { List }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut levels = List<u16>.make()
  run List<u16>.appendRepeated(&mut levels, 65535, 4) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if List<u16>.length(&levels) != 4 || List<u16>.get(&levels, 3) != 65535 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="List.impl.insertSlice"></a>

### Method `insertSlice`

```silk
pub effect fn insertSlice<T: Copy>(self: &mut Self, index: usize, values: &[T]) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Inserts a copy of each element of `values` at position `index`, in order, and moves the
elements from `index` onward `values.length` positions to the right.

#### When to use

Use `insertSlice` to insert many elements at once. It grows the list at most once and moves
the later elements with one overlapping copy, where one [`List.insert`](#List.impl.insert) for each element moves
them once per element.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the new storage. The list does not
  change.

#### Gotchas

If `index` is more than [`List.length`](#List.impl.length), the program traps.

#### Examples
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.collections.list { List }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut values = List<u16>.make()
  let ends: [u16; 2] = [1, 4]
  let middle: [u16; 2] = [2, 3]
  run List<u16>.appendSlice(&mut values, &ends) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run List<u16>.insertSlice(&mut values, 1, &middle) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if List<u16>.length(&values) != 4 || List<u16>.get(&values, 2) != 3 || List<u16>.get(&values, 3) != 4 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="List.impl.insertRepeated"></a>

### Method `insertRepeated`

```silk
pub effect fn insertRepeated<T: Copy>(self: &mut Self, index: usize, value: T, count: usize) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Inserts `count` copies of `value` at position `index` and moves the elements from `index`
onward `count` positions to the right.

#### Details

The list grows at most once, the later elements move with one overlapping copy, and the copies
are written in one tight loop. A `count` of 0 does nothing and does not allocate.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if `length + count` overflows `usize`, or the `Allocator` cannot supply
  the new storage. The list does not change.

#### Gotchas

If `index` is more than [`List.length`](#List.impl.length), the program traps.

#### Examples
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.collections.list { List }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut values = List<u16>.make()
  let ends: [u16; 2] = [1, 9]
  run List<u16>.appendSlice(&mut values, &ends) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run List<u16>.insertRepeated(&mut values, 1, 5, 3) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if List<u16>.length(&values) != 5 || List<u16>.get(&values, 3) != 5 || List<u16>.get(&values, 4) != 9 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```
